scope: Review of supplied plan; no experiments or model training performed.
assessment: Promising applied research on lightweight model-specific multilingual token budgeting. Browser resource savings and generalization remain hypotheses to measure.
corrections: The supplied baseline is ceil(chars/3.5), not 3.5 words per token. JavaScript string length measures UTF-16 code units; define baseline units explicitly and also record Unicode code points and UTF-8 bytes.
Conventional token-based model inference still requires the exact tokenizer to produce token IDs. A count estimator does not replace tokenization or increase the context window.

The inspected LocalMind commit explicitly says its real tokenizer resides in a worker inaccessible to the host token-count helper. Test exposing an exact count operation before attributing the problem to tokenizer size.
recommended_changes: Add browser baselines: exact count through existing worker, cached counts where serialization permits safe reuse, approximate count, and approximate screening followed by exact final prompt verification. Measure cold initialization, incremental download, memory, warm latency, worker messaging cost and main-thread blocking on actual target devices.

Evaluate downstream budgets on complete model-specific serialized prompts, including role delimiters, special tokens, system/tool content, generation prefix and reserved output. Content-only counts remain useful for RQ1/RQ2.

Prioritize overflow probability, overflow magnitude and retained history against an exact trimming oracle using the same retention policy. Undercount frequency alone does not distinguish a one-token error from a severe error.

Add a separate calibration split for upper estimates/safety margins; do not tune on devtest. Densest observed profile plus 15 percent is a heuristic and cannot guarantee safety on unseen inputs/tokenizers. A hypothetical estimate 20 percent below truth requires dividing by 0.8, not multiplying by 1.2.

Hold out tokenizer families and deduplicate identical tokenizer artifacts; splitting model names alone can leak a shared vocabulary. Keep parallel sentence IDs grouped across languages in independent train/calibration/test partitions where applicable.

Add emoji, combining marks, normalization variants, romanized Indic, mixed scripts, URLs, long identifiers, minified JSON, repeated punctuation, empty strings and long real chat-like text. Report short/long inputs separately; handle zero true tokens explicitly.

RQ3 should mean no target-tokenizer text fitting. File features do not specify future text frequencies. Normalize/decode vocabulary representations before Unicode classification; pin tokenizer_config and other runtime assets as well as tokenizer.json.
Treat native pre-tokenizer features as a tokenizer-assisted comparison and include their runtime dependency/cost. For fidelity, account for normalization preceding pre-tokenization.

Distinguish the plan introduction held-out -18/+37 result, phase-0 -16/+23 fixture result and commit comments about 42-sample fitting vs 38-sample fixtures. Record provenance before choosing a reproduction target.
Define 1 kB package measurement (compressed/uncompressed; profiles included) as an outcome, not a promise. Treat 2 weeks part-time as a pilot estimate, not a reliable full-study/publication schedule.
proposed_first_milestone: Reproduce the pinned LocalMind fixture test, establish JS/Python parity, and benchmark existing-worker exact counting versus the estimator for a small set of distinct tokenizer families and representative English, Indic, CJK, mixed-script and code inputs. Review phase 0 and phase 1 before later phases per source plan.
verified_by_inspection: LocalMind commit b39f0bc exists and contains the character baseline, per-script/per-model estimator and worker-access explanation.
